claim: The Sabah Trough is a foredeep/flexural moat in the same Dangerous Grounds crust, bent down under wedge load; it has no independent tectonic origin.
Foredeep onset at COLLISION_MM is difficult to trace because the same event is erosional on the wedge side but onlap/condensation/facies-change in the moat.
source: Arif ENTERPRISE relay 2026-09-30 (unconformity landward, conformity basinward)

claim: Some Middle–Late Miocene apparent regional sequence boundaries in this position are mobile-substrate accommodation surfaces rather than tectonic or eustatic boundaries.
source: Public mobile-shale work + ENTERPRISE relay 2026-09-30 (Pagasa wedge mini-basins/canopy 13–10.5 Ma)

claim: Hiatus behaviour across the trough is a time-gap field: durations vary well-to-well, surfaces merge, become condensed sections, or disappear — never a single instantaneous basinwide line.
source: Chronosequence method (Krebs, via ENTERPRISE relay) + well graphic-correlation record
